paper_title: Influence of Molecular Geometry of Perylene Diimide Dimers and Polymers on Bulk Heterojunction Morphology Toward High-Performance Nonfullerene Polymer Solar Cells
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Adv Funct Materials - 2015 - Wu - Influence of Molecular Geometry of Perylene Diimide Dimers and Polymers on Bulk/auto/Adv Funct Materials - 2015 - Wu - Influence of Molecular Geometry of Perylene Diimide Dimers and Polymers on Bulk.md

knowledge_points.content: B-di-PDI is a bay-linked perylene diimide dimer characterized by a flexible structure with a 70° torsion angle between the two PDI units, whereas H-di-PDI is a hydrazine-linked dimer with a rigid structure and a 90° torsion angle.
knowledge_points.evidence: In this study, the relatively flexible B-di-PDI acceptor having a 70° torsion angle between the two constituent PDI units was used to compare with the rigid H-di-PDI acceptor which has a 90° torsion angle.

knowledge_points.content: The polymer solar cell based on the PTB7-Th:H-di-PDI blend achieved a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 6.41%, with a short-circuit current (Jsc) of 13.12 mA cm⁻², an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.79 V, and a fill factor (FF) of 0.60.
knowledge_points.evidence: the PTB7-Th:H-di-PDI device delivered an even higher PCEMAX of 6.41% with a Jsc of 13.12 mA cm−2, a Voc of 0.79 V, and an FF of 0.60.

knowledge_points.content: The pseudo 2D conjugated polymer PTB7-Th exhibits better miscibility with both B-di-PDI and H-di-PDI acceptors compared to its 1D analog PTB7, due to the presence of conjugated side chains that facilitate effective donor-acceptor interactions.

(PTB7-Th) has better miscibility with both bay-linked di-PDI (B-di-PDI) and hydrazine-linked di-PDI (H-di-PDI) compared to its 1D analog... (PTB7) ...conjugated side chains of these polymers can facilitate better compatibility.

knowledge_points.content: GIWAXS analysis indicates that the flexible and twisted structure of B-di-PDI severely disrupts the face-on oriented π-π stacking of PTB7-Th, while the rigid H-di-PDI maintains the polymer's stacking intensity, facilitating better charge transport.
knowledge_points.evidence: The PTB7-Th:H-di-PDI film shows a comparable peak intensity of the face-on oriented π-π stacking to that of the neat PTB7-Th film, whereas the PTB7-Th:B-di-PDI film exhibits a lower peak intensity of the face-on oriented π-π stacking.

knowledge_points.content: In PTB7-Th:di-PDI nonfullerene solar cells, the electron mobility (μe) is the performance-limiting factor because the hole mobility (μh) is consistently higher across the studied blend films.
knowledge_points.evidence: As shown, all the BHJ films exhibited higher μh than μe, indicating that μe is the limiting factor for achieving high Jsc and FF.

knowledge_points.content: The optimal bulk heterojunction morphology for di-PDI based devices was achieved using a 1:1 donor-to-acceptor ratio and a solvent mixture containing 1 vol% 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO) and 2 vol% 1-chloronaphthalene (CN).
knowledge_points.evidence: The optimized donor/acceptor (D/A) ratio for all nonfullerene BHJs is 1:1 with 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO) (1 vol%) and 1-chloronaphthalene (CN) (2 vol%) as solvent additives to promote optimal BHJ morphology.

knowledge_points.content: The external quantum efficiency (EQE) of the top-performing PTB7-Th:H-di-PDI device reached a peak value of 70% at 540 nm.
knowledge_points.evidence: Impressively, the highest EQE value of the top-performing PTB7-Th:H-di-PDI device reaches 70% at 540 nm.

knowledge_points.content: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) revealed that the PTB7:H-di-PDI blend film has a high root mean square roughness (Rrms) of 3.22 nm, indicating excessive phase separation and poor intermixing compared to PTB7-Th blends.
knowledge_points.evidence: It was revealed that the PTB7:H-di-PDI film possesses the roughest surface with a root mean square roughness (Rrms) of 3.22 nm... indicating that inferior intermixing between H-di-PDI and 1D PTB7.

knowledge_points.content: The rigid geometry of H-di-PDI allows it to maintain appropriate aggregation domains within the PTB7-Th matrix, which provides suitable percolation pathways for charge transport while still enabling efficient exciton dissociation.
knowledge_points.evidence: The H-di-PDI acceptor could not only mix well with PTB7-Th but also maintained appropriate aggregation domains to facilitate efficient exciton dissociation and suitable percolation pathways for charge transport.

knowledge_points.content: Steady-state photoluminescence (PL) quenching measurements show that the PTB7-Th:H-di-PDI blend achieved 95% hole transfer quenching and 92% electron transfer quenching, signifying high exciton dissociation efficiency.
